courseTitle: 100 Days of Code: JavaScript Data Structures and Algorithms

cues.en: Now in this lecture we are going to look at common stack operations.
So these are the operations that we can perform in JavaScript for stack.
So we are going to perform push pop.
Peek is empty size and delete all methods.
Now let's look at them one by one.
Then we are going to implement them using array and using linked list.
So basically we are going to implement the stack data structure in two ways by using the arrays and
linked list.
Now the first operation is push operation.
Now push means that we are inserting elements to the stack.
Now in this case when we are pushing the elements, the next element that we are going to push is going
to locate it on the top of the previous one.
And this is going to continue like this to maintain the first in, last out approach.
So until we reach the end.
So every time when we are inserting the element we are going to call this pushing the element.
It's going to push on the top of the previous element.
Then we have the pop method.
Now in case of pop method, when we are popping the elements, this means that it's going to remove
the elements and return that element.
So here we cannot remove the first element that we have inserted or we cannot remove any random element.
Every time when we remove the element, we can only remove the last inserted element from the stack.
So to maintain the LFO method, we have to do it like this.
So whenever we call the pop method, it's going to remove the last element and return that element.
Now if I call it one more time, it's going to remove the one more time last element.
So if I call it one more time in this case the last element is 20, it's going to remove it like this
until we have reached the last element.
Now the next method that we are going to implement is going to be the peak method.
Now peak method is kind of similar to the pop method.
But in this case we are not removing the element from the stack, we are just returning the last inserted
element from the stack.
Now in this case, if we call peak method, it's going to return 40, but the 40 will remain in the
stack.
Now you might be interested.
Why do we need a method like this?
Now in some application, we just might check the top element in the stack without removing it.
In this case we are going to use the peak method.
Now the next operation is going to be the checking that if the stack is empty or not.
So in this case our stack is not empty.
We have elements.
So if we you have one or more than elements in the stack, it's not going to be empty.
If you don't have it, it's going to be empty.
So in this case it's empty.
Method is going to return false.
Now in some programming language we are implementing the full method.
But in case of JavaScript it's full method is not needed because we don't have any limitation for the
number of elements in the array.
So we can insert as many as elements in the array or link this.
That's why our stack will not be full.
Now the next method is going to be the size.
So this is going to return the number of the elements in the stack.
So in this case it's going to be the four because we have four elements.
Then the last method is going to be the delete all.
So we can call it clear or delete all.
So it doesn't matter whatever you name it.
So whenever we are calling clear or delete all method, it's going to delete all elements from the stack
and the stack will be empty.
Now as I mentioned before, we are going to implement the stack in two ways using arrays and using linked
list.
Now in the next lecture we will continue to implement the stack with all these operations using array,
because in interviews they are asking this implementation as well the approach that you are going to
implement.
And we are going to implement the linked list as well.
So see you in the next lecture.
